title: Selectivity strong-nucleophile lookup misses solved aqueous base inventory

first_api_refusal.classification: register session directive excluded by API; no chemistry executed; preserved independently

observations.primary: SO-001 cool/hot and SO-003 primary retain all 0.0002 mol substrate and emit the named primary + weak nucleophile refusal; no solver_failed event occurs.
observations.tertiary: SO-003 tertiary strong-base forecast E2 instead selects SN1 and yields 0.0002 mol tert-butanol. It consumes water and forms bromide/acid, subsequently neutralized by existing analytical base.
observations.controls: SO-002 neutral tertiary SN1 and SO-004 neutral cool SN1 / hot E1 principal forecasts are met; no physical calibration claim.
observations.closure: All seven explicit React comparisons close H/C/O/Na/Br/charge (plus atmospheric N) within the frozen 1e-8 mol tolerance when authoritative analytical basis and gas transfers are counted. No missing mass is demonstrated.

source_diagnosis.lookup: selectivity.rs NUCLEOPHILES lists literal NaOH then water; find_nucleophile tests vessel.moles_of(key) > 1e-12. Before React, NaOH is zero while Na+ and base_equivalents remain, so lookup falls back to water and chooses the weak class.
source_diagnosis.ownership_limit: Analytical base_equivalents is an OH stoichiometric inventory coordinate, not measured free hydroxide. A fix must prove eligible finite hydroxide/reaction ownership and debit conservative pools; it cannot relabel arbitrary alkalinity or sodium as NaOH.
source_diagnosis.not_allowed: Do not inject raw NaOH, reorder React before solving, change counterions, relax the physical forecast, invent rate/heat or silently make general salts strongly nucleophilic.

required_acceptance_lanes.tasks: Compare the same finite NaOH dose before and after authoritative aqueous solving: primary cool SN2 / hot E2 and tertiary strong-base E2. Require matching product/debit/Na/Br/H/O/charge and interpretation of the threshold from actual temperature; no duplicate endpoint.

NaBr/NaCl/sodium-only waters must not become strong base; neutral/sour water must retain the appropriate tertiary SN1/E1 behavior. Carbonate and weak-base analytical alkalinity must not silently become hydroxide. Test finite base exhaustion, partial neutralization and no eligible base.

Insufficient owned base constrains extent. Refused, unsupported and failed transformed-readback paths preserve initial matter/events atomically. Preserve named partial scope; do not mutate global thermal policy.

Canonical ionic coproducts must be available to the next operation. Closure includes actual gas export/retention and initial trapped air. Require equivalent native/core/Wasm/API behavior, exact source/binary/lock bindings and no empirical rate/heat claim.

execution_policy: No new runs in this intake; four adapted requests completed once, original 422 preserved. Model source unchanged; no shared index edits.
